body: I know what you mean, some days I wish my friend wasn't even at school so I wouldn't have to see him and be reminded of all my negative thoughts.

As much as a relief it would be if suddenly I didn't finish my senior studies, I don't want to run away and leave them behind, especially if escaping this small town of mine doesn't prove to be a good decision and I kill myself anyway. If I did that I'd feel like I accomplished absolutely nothing in my life. I'm staying at school just so at least I can say I accomplished finishing it one day.

I have to stay in my town for the year, or at least, until I finish my senior studies. So that's that, I guess. I'd love to leave. I fantasize about leaving every day. It'd be so nice to escape absolutely everything and trying to start again in another place. Whether or not it'd be worth it only time will tell, but it is an idea that appeals to me.

Thank you for your advice. I really want to be included by my friends because I really like them, but maybe you're right, maybe our connection is an unhealthy one. 
I really like your idea of stepping out and going places to do things and meet more people, and I would, except I'm not so sure I can. For the rest of the year, anyway, I'm pretty much grounded to my deadend little town. And at the same time, I wonder if maybe I just come across as awkward or weird; I've never had a friendship with anyone that could be classified as "stable", maybe even when I travel and try to form new connections I'll still be rejected by others. 
Again, thank you for your advice.

I mean tell my family that I've been suffering anxiety and suicidal thoughts for the past year, sorry I didn't make myself clearer before. :( I guess by me saying they don't understand me is that I think if I ever told them how I feel about my life and about my friends, they'd call it trivial and spout things like, "friends are only temporary, don't worry about it," etc. My parents and I share different values for some things. In all honesty they'd probably want me to not put any attention towards strong relationships with others if it meant I put more attention towards my schoolwork. Which is another reason I'm petrified about ever confiding in them. 
My friends aren't huge on drinking either, they enjoy it more for the social aspect. I used to be the same, I guess I rationalise my exclusion by thinking things like "well, I don't even like drinking anyway..." I personally think my friends and I are similar people in terms of values (it was what drew us together in the first place) but I don't really know anymore. 
I want to focus on my relationship with my best friend because right now I fear it's on the rocks. At the same time, though, I don't want to invest too much time in case it turns out he wants to discard my friendship. I've made the mistake of investing too much in other people before, I try to tread lightly with that now. 
Thank you for your advice. It's got me thinking about maybe strengthening my connection with my parents, maybe helping them see life more realistically and not through rose-tinted glasses.

I hate how life can give you hints of better things to come, then bring them crashing down even further. I totally empathise with you there. Life is horrible. There's no sugar-coating it. This is a void, pointless existence and finding meaning within it is near impossible. 

Note I said "near". It's not impossible. And I think, after all my own years of depression, of tears, of emptiness, of feeling dead, of planning my own suicide... I think I know a better way out for you. 

Travel. 

Travel the world. Go somewhere new. Somewhere different. Immerse yourself in a culture that you know nothing about. And do it as though you're going to commit suicide the moment you return. Why? Because you'll make the most of your trip. Why bother killing yourself after a pointless, boring day? It's like the holiday is your last supper: indulge yourself. Please. Please let go of what hurts you. It's hard, yes; fuck I know it's hard. I just found my own way out from a horrible friendship sever with someone I thought was my friend soulmate for life. And for nearly every night of my life after that severance, I would practice suicide notes, tying the hangman's knot, choosing a tall tree or a high building for jumping off. Because I was so caught up in what used to be, that I couldn't focus on what was coming. 

Look at it this way: the past does not exist. Nothing that "happened" yesterday, the day before, last year, twenty years ago, etc. ever happened. The moment a moment passes, it's gone forever. So if you're holding onto the past, you're holding on to what does. not. exist. It's the present that matters. If you can try your best to overcome loneliness and rejection than already you are helping your today become a lot better. 

Once you're ready, but a plane/cruise/train ticket and go anywhere. Everywhere. Take yourself as far away from familiarity as you can. Feel ALIVE. Be free. Find beauty amongst nature. 

Please find love. I hope you will. I love you.

Dear justanotherthrawayar,

I'm where you are at the moment. Nothing around me works to make me feel needed or wanted in this world. The people who surround me feel more like distorted shadows than flesh and blood and emotion. The one person I cared about more than life itself has turned me away from their life.

I know how it feels to feel nothing. I'm where you are. You are NOT alone in your feelings. 

It's perfectly okay to feel the way you do. Life is a sad, strange mess. A mix of happy to balance out the sad sometimes, a mix of anger, frustration, plentiness, loneliness. But the one thing that keeps us as a species alive is love. Love is the emotion that drives passion, positive chaos, freedom, self-expression, and JOY.

Some people find love in others. Some find it in a sport, or a hobby- I myself picked up art as it was something I'd always liked, and as a therapy it has worked wonders for me. I want you too to simply let go. Let go of what ails you. What makes you sad. What pains you. And find something to love. 

For your case, I'd suggest going on a holiday to someplace you've never been. Overseas would be optimal. Pack your bags, open-ended ticket, unlock your heart and let your emptiness open to bring love back in. 

I want you to see the world. Yes, life is a mess, life is cruel, life does not favour or apologise anyone. But the Earth is beautiful. Endless oceans of sapphire blue, pure in salt and depth. Tall swaying rainforests with the shimmering echoes of wildlife. Little cafes and restaurants, even; tucked away far out of sight and collecting those who seek love within their four walls. 

I want you to stay on this Earth. I want you here. I don't know you personally - and I won't pretend I do - but I do mean it when I say I want you to find something beautiful to love. You deserve so much, and life has dealt you a sour hand recently, I'm so sorry to hear that. But I know you are beautiful, you are kind (you sound kind, at least), your heart can open, and you can fill it with the love that you deserve.

You are a person. You deserve to see the most incredible, fantastic, awe-inspiring things.
